summary: Wataru Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota. Ryose also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

Wayne Chandira is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. As attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Rowe.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a Master of Theology and a Ph.D. from Harvard University. He taught at Fordham University (~1970–1972) and served as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1972–2018).

Wei Lin, a scholar of sinology and archaeology, earned a Ph.D. from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Lin worked as an archaeologist at Nanjing Municipal Museum and held posts at Ohio State, Michigan, Western Michigan, and Transylvania University.
Wei Wu is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Buddhist College. Attested in 2026, Wu is an Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

Wei-Cheng Lin works in history and archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Lin was a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015 and joined the faculty of the University of Chicago in 2015.

Wei-jen Teng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Teng has taught at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute.

Wei-ming Tu is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University. He held positions at Princeton, UC Berkeley, East-West Center, Harvard University, and Harvard-Yenching Institute, along with several visiting professorships.
Weijue Shi (1928–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who was ordained under Linyuan in 1963. He founded Chung Tai Shan, Lin Quan Temple (1987), and the Chung Tai Buddhist Institute (1993).
Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Shen held teaching posts at the University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China (~2006–2015).
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. Huang was affiliated with the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and holds a professorship at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin is a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology who studied under Fang-Kuei Li (~1968–1972). He served as a professor at the University of Iowa from around 1973, later becoming Professor Emeritus of Chinese.

Wen-ling Jane is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2009), also studying under Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai is an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned a PhD at Peking University and studied at Kyoto and Hamburg. Mai served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek, a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, earned a PhD from Stanford in 1998. She held a post at Barnard College and became Professor and Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.

Wendy Doniger is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history who earned Ph.D.s from Harvard and Oxford. In 1978, she joined the University of Chicago, serving as the Mircea Eliade Distinguished Service Professor Emerita.
Wenjiang Ding (1887–1936) was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied under Qichao Liang (~1902–1911) and at Peking University, where he later held a post around 1913.

Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar who studied at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts. He held several leadership roles at Dunhuang Academy between 1946 and 1998, including Director.
Wenjie Qin is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu.
